questions.question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 - Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying, etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

(9, 3, 90)

(5, 4, 41)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

**Logic: **(First number)² + (Second number)² = Third number

 
• (9, 3, 90) → 9² + 3² = 81 + 9 = 90
 
• (5, 4, 41) → 52 + 42 = 25 + 16 = 41

Similarly,

 
• (13, 7, 218) → 132 + 72 = 169 + 49 = 218

Hence, '**(13, 7, 218)**' is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the word-pair that best represents a similar relationship to the one expressed in the pair of words given below.

(The words must be considered meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/consonants/vowels in the word.)

Blaze ∶ Eruption
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

**Logic:** Words are synonym of each other.

 
• Blaze ∶ Eruption → Blaze is synonym of eruption.

Similarly,

 
• Bony ∶ Haggard → Bony is synonym of haggard.

Hence, '**Bony ∶ Haggard**' is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some hockeys are bats.

All bats are racquets.

No stick is a racquet.

**Conclusions:**

(I) Some sticks are bats.

(II) Some sticks are hockeys is a possibility.

(III) All hockeys are racquets.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow
Both conclusions II and III follow

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram is: 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/15c6afb73beb0056ccb19281e947110bae87d087a39098d9c865be9c912aacc4.png] 

Conclusions:

(I) Some sticks are bats. → Does not follow (As, All bats are racquets and No stick is a racquet, which implies No sticks are bats)

(II) Some sticks are hockeys is a possibility. → **Follows** (There is no definite relation between sticks and hockeys, so it is a possibility that some sticks are hockeys)

(III) All hockeys are racquets. → Does not follow (As, Some hockeys are bats and All bats are racquets, which implies some hockeys are racquets)

Hence, '**Only conclusion II follows**' is the correct answer.

**Statements:**

All surgeons are therapists.

questions.question: If 29 November 2009 is Sunday, then what will be the day of the week on 30 May 2010?
questions.solution:
There are 2 odd days in a month with 30 days and 3 odd days in a month with 31 days. Also, February with 28 days has 0 odd days and February with 29 days have 1 odd day.

Number of odd days between 29 November 2009 to 30 May 2010 = (1 + 3 + 3 + 0 + 3 + 2 + 30) = 42

42 when divided by 7, leaves 0 as remainder.

Sunday + 0 = Sunday

Hence, ‘**Sunday**’ is the correct answer.

Four triads of numbers have been given out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the one that is different.

questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

**Logic:** First number + 20 = Second number; Second number + 20 = Third number

 
• 25 - 45 - 65 → 25 + 20 = 45; 45 + 20 = 65
 
• 8 - 28 - 48 → 8 + 20 = 28; 28 + 20 = 48
 
• 38 - 58 - 78 → 38 + 20 = 58; 58 + 20 = 78
 
• **17 - 27 - 67 → 17 + 10 = 27; 27 + 40 = 67**

Hence, '**17 - 27 - 67**' is the correct answer.
